Based on the chest X-ray findings, which of the following options best describes the characteristics and potential diagnosis of the mediastinal mass observed in the patient’s radiograph?

A) The mass is calcified and located in the right paratracheal region, suggesting a focal pattern of fibrosing mediastinitis.
B) The mass is non-calcified, located in the anterior mediastinum, indicating a diffuse pattern of fibrosing mediastinitis.
C) The mass is calcified, located in the anterior mediastinum, which is typical for a germinal cell neoplasm.
D) The mass is non-calcified, located in the right paratracheal region, suggesting a diffuse pattern of fibrosing mediastinitis.
E) The mass is non-calcified, located in the anterior mediastinum, which is typical for a thymoma.
F) The mass is calcified and located in the anterior mediastinum, suggesting a focal pattern of fibrosing mediastinitis.
